assertions.text: Output contains at least one markdown table (using | column | syntax)
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Name | Email | Dietary Requirements | Accessibility Needs | Valid? | Rejection Reason? |

assertions.text: Email validation and name-required scenarios are present — at least one row for invalid email and one for missing name.
assertions.evidence: | Missing email | Jane Doe | | | | no | Invalid email format |

assertions.text: Dietary requirements and/or accessibility needs use blank cells when the attendee has not provided them (genuinely absent) — not 'N/A' or 'none'.
assertions.evidence: | Missing name, regardless of other fields | | valid@example.com | {Vegetarian, (none)} | {Wheelchair access, (none)} | no | Name is required |

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Accepted?', 'Price?')
Scenario names describe conditions ('Missing email', 'Early-bird single attendee') — not outcomes ('Rejected', 'Discounted').
assertions.evidence: | Missing name, regardless of other fields | ... | Whitespace-only name | ... | Email missing @ symbol |

assertions.text: The discount stacking ambiguity (early-bird + group) is surfaced as an open question — not silently resolved.
assertions.evidence: ### Open Question: Discount Stacking ... Flag this for confirmation before implementation

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Name | Email | Dietary Requirements | Accessibility Needs | Valid? | Rejection Reason? |

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: ## Table 1: Registration Validity ... ## Table 2: Registration Price Calculation

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 has 9 rows focused on validity; Table 2 has 7 rows focused on pricing

assertions.text: Input validation rules and pricing/discount calculation are in separate tables
assertions.evidence: Two separate concerns here: **validity of a registration** and **price calculation**.

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values (e.g. 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff') rather than raw dates — making the table readable without knowing the actual cutoff date.
assertions.evidence: Registration Date column uses raw dates like '2026-07-01', '2026-05-15', not descriptive terms.

assertions.text: If registration date uses descriptive values like 'before cutoff', the cutoff date is not also present as a separate column (it's already encoded in the description). Numeric policy thresholds like min group size are acceptable as columns since they are configuration values worth discussing with business experts.
assertions.evidence: Since dates are raw, not descriptive, the conditional rule is vacuously satisfied; cutoff column 'Early-Bird Cutoff (Policy)' pairs with raw dates rather than a descriptive-only encoding.

assertions.text: The minimum group size threshold appears as a policy column (e.g. 'Min group size (policy)') — surfacing this as a configurable business rule, not just implied by the boundary rows.
assertions.evidence: | Group Threshold (Policy) | ... | 5 |' column explicitly surfaces the min group size as a policy value.
